etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English supporten, from Old French supporter, from Latin supportō.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To help keep from falling.

quote.citation: 1995, Nancy Berliner, Sarah Handler, Friends of the House‎[1], →ISBN, page 79:
quote.text: There is a soft-mat seat (which originally had a palm fiber underwebbing) supported by three curved transverse braces.

One of the keys to glassing effectively is supporting your binoculars. Advanced glassers who scan lots of country for long periods of time, or who use binoculars of 10X power or more, often use a lightweight camera tripod  […]

definitions.definition: (transitive) To back or favor a cause, party, etc., mentally or with concrete aid.
(transitive) To help, particularly financially; to subsidize.

quote.citation: 2020 April 14, “Beaten into a Coma for My Faith, Recovered Without Medical Treatment”, in Minghui‎[2]:
quote.text: I said I shouldn’t support anything that deceives people.

quote.citation: 2023 August 2, Ben Tinker, Meg Tirrell and Brenda Goodman, “New director named at National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases after Fauci’s retirement”, in CNN‎[3]:
quote.text: The NIAID supports projects at universities and research organizations around the United States as well as a network of 21 NIAID labs across the country.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To provide evidence for; to lend credibility to.

quote.citation: 1754, Jonathan Edwards, The Freedom of the Will:
quote.text: to urge such arguments, as though they were sufficient to support and demonstrate a whole scheme of moral philosophy

definitions.definition: (transitive) To serve, as in a customer-oriented position; to give support to.
(transitive) To assist or be involved with, but not be responsible for.
(transitive) To answer questions and resolve problems regarding something sold.
(transitive, said of electronic devices, programming languages, etc.) To be designed to provide capacity for; to work or be compatible with (a part, accessory, file type, program, algorithm, etc.).
(transitive, archaic) To endure without being overcome; bear; undergo; tolerate.

quote.citation: 1681, John Dryden, The Spanish Fryar: Or, the Double Discovery. […], London:  […]  Richard Tonson and Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC, (please specify the page number):
quote.text: This fierce demeanour and his insolence / The patience of a god could not support.
For a strong affection such moments are worth supporting, and they will end well; for your advocate is in your lover's heart and speaks her own language […]

definitions.definition: (transitive) To play a lesser part in the same production with (a star performer).

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English support, from Anglo-Norman and Middle French support. Displaced Old English wraþu.

definitions.definition: (sometimes attributive) Something which supports.
Financial or other help.

quote.citation: 2011 December 19, Kerry Brown, “Kim Jong-il obituary”, in The Guardian‎[4]:
quote.text: Kim was educated at the newly founded university in Pyongyang, named after his father, graduating in 1964. The 1960s and early 1970s were the golden years for the DPRK. It undertook rapid industrialisation, economically outstripped its southern competitor, and enjoyed the support of both the People's Republic of China, and the Soviet Union.

quote.citation: 2012, BioWare, Mass Effect 3 (Science Fiction), Redwood City: Electronic Arts, →OCLC, PC, scene: Normandy SR-2:
quote.text: Admiral Hackett: Hell of a thing you just pulled off, Commander. Curing the genophage? I never thought I'd see the day.Shepard: Wrex has agreed to help the turians, Admiral. We should get their full support.

definitions.definition: Answers to questions and resolution of problems regarding something sold.
(mathematics) in relation to a function, the set of points where the function is not zero; the closure of that set.
(fuzzy set theory) A set whose elements are at least partially included in a given fuzzy set (i.e., whose grade of membership in that fuzzy set is strictly greater than zero).
Evidence.
(computing) Compatibility and functionality for a given product or feature.
An actor playing a subordinate part with a star.
An accompaniment in music.
(gymnastics) Clipping of support position.

quote.citation: 2008, Christopher Sommer, Building the Gymnastic Body, the Science of Gymnastic Strength Training, page 88:
quote.text: Dip down as far as you are able, aiming to descend to the bottom of your sternum. Press back up to a support.

definitions.definition: (structural analysis) Horizontal, vertical or rotational support of structures: movable, hinged, fixed. (Can we add an example for this sense?)
